summary: Peter Kuhlmann is a linguist who earned his doctorate under Rosemarie L'u00fchr (~1990–1993). He held posts at the University of Giessen (~1997–2002), the University of D'u00fcsseldorf (~2002–2004), and the University of G'u00f6ttingen (~2004).

Peter Lindegger-Stauffer was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as curator at the Tibet Institute Rikon (1967–1974) and received an honorary Ph.D. from the University of Fribourg in ~1998.

Peter M. Scharf is an Indologist and linguist who completed his Ph.D. under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania (1983–1990). He founded the Sanskrit Library in 2002 and held appointments at Brown University, IIIT Hyderabad, and IIAS.
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under L. P. N. Perera and completed his doctorate under Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Tufts University and completed a Ph.D. at the University of Washington under Charles Keyes. His teachers also included Leonard van der Kuijp and several traditional Tibetan masters.

Peter N. Gregory is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi (1981). He held posts at UIUC (attested 1986–1994), Smith College (attested 2005), and the Kuroda Institute.

Peter Nicolas Harting was an Indologist and linguist who completed his M.A. and Ph.D. at Utrecht University under Willem Caland. He held lectureships in London and Oxford before becoming Professor of English at Groningen (1925–1937) and Amsterdam (1937–1962).

Peter Percival was an Indologist and linguist who served as Principal of Jaffna Central College (1832–1851). In 1856, he became Registrar at the University of Madras and Professor of Sanskrit and Vernacular Literature at Presidency University.

Peter Peterson was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, under Aufrecht, Müller, and Monier-Williams. He served as Sanskrit Professor at Elphinstone College and Registrar at the University of Mumbai (~1873–1899).

Peter Schreiner is an Indologist who earned his doctorate under Paul Hacker at the University of Münster (~1969–1972) and completed his Habilitation at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich (1990).
Peter Schwabland is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his M.A. at the University of Washington in 1994 under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and completed his Promotion (1982) and Habilitation (1995) at the University of Bonn. He was appointed to the chair of Tibetology at the University of Bonn in 2001.

Peter Scott Noble was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Aberdeen and Cambridge. He was Professor of Latin at Leeds (1930–1938), Professor of Humanity at Aberdeen (1938–1952), Principal of King's College London, and Vice-Chancellor of London University.

Peter Skilling is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at the EPHE (2004). He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and has held posts at EFEO, Chulalongkorn University, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Peter Stewart is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who earned his degrees at Clare College, Cambridge. He worked at Cambridge, Reading, and the Courtauld Institute before becoming Associate Professor at Oxford and head of the Classical Art Research Centre in 2011.

Peter Stumpf was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. under Werner Thomas at Goethe University Frankfurt (1959–1968), where he subsequently served as an assistant until 1977.
Peter Thomi is an Indologist who studied under Alfred Bloch. He served as the head of the Institut für Indologie Wichtrach (attested 1995).

Peter Zieme is a specialist in Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist linguistics who studied at Humboldt University (1960–1965). He worked at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR and later led Turfan research at the BBAW (~1992–2007).

Peter van der Veer is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Sinology who earned his doctorate from Utrecht University. He held professorships at Amsterdam, Utrecht, and Göttingen, and served as Director of the Max Planck Institute (MMG) from ~2009 to 2021.

Peter von Bohlen was an Indologist who studied at Halle, Bonn, and Berlin under Gesenius, Schlegel, Freytag, and Bopp. He spent his career at the University of Königsberg, becoming an ordinary professor of oriental literature in 1828/1830.
